name: Behavioral Pricing: Insights, Methods, and Strategy
description:
In this seminar, classical pricing approaches and tools will be presented and discussed. In contrast to these, “Behavioral Pricing” based on insights from “Behavioral Economics” will be introduced. On the basis of numerous case studies from different sectors (FMCG, client services, capital investments) and markets (B2C versus B2B) methodological implications and strategic options will be developed to examine how “Behavioral Pricing” can be effectively leveraged in practice.

The seminar is designed as a “block-seminar” with an extensive introduction to be given at the kick-off event and several break-out case studies throughout the remaining days. Furthermore, participants will be assigned to small groups in the beginning and will focus on a specific topic which they research, elaborate and present in the course of the seminar. Presentations will be held on the block days and active participation in discussions is expected from all participants of the seminar. At the end each group also hands-in a final written seminar paper.

Seminar participants have to be present at all seminar dates (prerequisite for passing, no exceptions will be made!), engage in the discussions and ideally should be willing to share and discuss their practical experience in pricing or pricing-related fields. We explicitly encourage participation of students who are already advanced in their Master studies.
prerequisites: Practical experience with pricing and pricing-related topics is very helpful, students should be open to share and discuss their practical experience.
